title: PRD: Modular endpoint profiles (per-route QoS + telemetry-driven degradation) and launch checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: Enable modular endpoint profiles for hosted inference so product teams can attach per-route quality, latency and cost targets plus an automated degradation policy that triggers telemetry-driven fallback behavior. This PRD covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, metrics, and a detailed launch checklist for the MVP.
background: Customers running production LLM features need predictable latency and predictable unit economics. Today hosted endpoints expose a single surface-level configuration. That forces either conservative defaults (higher cost) or brittle client-side fallbacks. We will ship endpoint profiles: a lightweight object attached to an endpoint defining QoS targets, allowed fallbacks, and telemetry triggers that the routing/control plane uses to enforce graceful degradation.
goals: Allow per-endpoint profiles to express SLO targets (p95 latency), max per-token cost guidance, and a graded fallback sequence
Operate degradation automatically based on telemetry signals (latency spikes, error rate, capacity pressure), with configurable thresholds
Provide visibility in Console and API: profile contracts, recent degradation events, and token-level cost/latency breakdowns
Ship a minimal rollout path with canary, regional opt-in, and manual override controls
non_goals: Full policy engine for arbitrary routing rules (out of scope for MVP)
Per-customer custom kernels or model re-quantization scheduling (handled by runtime roadmaps)
Replacing Reserved/Dedicated capacity model; profiles will integrate with Dedicated but not alter billing model
scope_included: API: create/read/update/delete endpoint profiles via Redwood API and SDK
Console: profile creation UI, profile assignment to hosted endpoints, profile dashboard showing recent triggers
Control plane: evaluate telemetry signals, mark endpoint degraded, select fallback model variant from profile rules
Telemetry: new metrics and events (profile_evaluation, profile_degradation_start/end, fallback_selected)
Rollout: canary traffic targeting and manual pause/resume controls
scope_out_of_scope: On-prem control plane changes beyond telemetry ingestion contract
Deep model-level quality evaluation (that remains in Optimize/eval pipelines)
Automated billing adjustments or dynamic pricing—only guidance will be surfaced
user_stories: As an app owner I want to attach a 'low-latency' profile to my chat endpoint so the platform automatically falls back to a faster model variant when p95 > 500ms
As a platform engineer I want to see a timeline of degradation events in Console to correlate with infra incidents
As an SRE I want an automated rollback that restores pre-degradation routing when latency returns below threshold
requirements: REQ-API-1: Endpoint profiles must be creatable via POST /v1/endpoint_profiles with JSON schema (id, name, targets, fallbacks, evaluation_window_seconds, thresholds)
REQ-API-2: Assign profile to endpoint via endpoint config; assignment is atomic and versioned
REQ-RUNTIME-1: Control plane must evaluate profile triggers at a configurable cadence (default 10s) using p95 and error-rate over last N seconds
REQ-RUNTIME-2: When a degradation is triggered, select the first compatible fallback model listed in the profile using routing policy (region, tier, model-compatibility)
REQ-CONSOLE-1: Profile UI must allow preflight simulation against historical telemetry for the target endpoint
REQ-OBS-1: Emit structured events for all profile evaluations and state transitions to the telemetry pipeline
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Create/assign/delete profile flows succeed via API and Console; assignment shows in endpoint metadata
AC-2: Profile evaluation triggers when p95 exceeds threshold for configured window; endpoint switches to fallback and traffic routes as expected
AC-3: The Console shows degradation timeline and which fallback model was selected with links to relevant logs
AC-4: Can initiate a controlled canary roll (1% traffic) to validate profile before full rollout
AC-5: No more than 0.1% increase in 99th-percentile request errors across platform caused by the new control plane behavior during a staged rollout
AC-6: Telemetry events documented and available in downstream analytics (events retained per observability retention policy)
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only profile creation and simulated evaluations against synthetic telemetry
Beta: customer opt-in via Console (select beta flag) + 1% canary traffic for opted endpoints
Staged: region-by-region (us-west-2 -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1), increasing traffic 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%
Rollback criteria: doubled error-rate, >2x expected latency on fallback, or >10% increase in token spend beyond projected guidance
GA: open to all new hosted endpoints + migration tool to attach profiles to existing endpoints using suggested defaults
launch_checklist: API: public API spec published, example SDK snippets in JS and Python
Console: profile creation flow validated in staging and UAT; beta flag available
Runtime: evaluation cadence and fallback logic performance validated under 5000 rps synthetic load
Telemetry: events flowing to Observability pipeline; dashboards created (profile health, active degradations)
Docs: PRD converted to public-facing guide 'Endpoint profiles and graceful degradation'
Security: brief security review completed (no new IAM surface exposed), approval from Security
Billing/Legal: confirm no billing changes; update TOS guidance on behavior-driven fallbacks
SRE/On-call: Runbook for profile-induced degradations published and paged test verified
Support: knowledge base article and canned responses for customers experiencing degradation
Training: short internal demo and release notes distributed to Solutions and Sales
risks: Risk-1: Fallbacks could have significantly different quality characteristics and break user experience
Risk-2: Telemetry windows too short or noisy, causing oscillation between degraded and normal states
Risk-3: Control plane latency in deciding fallbacks could add overhead to request path
Risk-4: Customers may be surprised by automatic fallback without clear visibility
mitigations: Mitigation-1: Profile must allow quality annotation and an explicit ‘do_not_fallback’ flag for critical endpoints
Mitigation-2: Hysteresis: require N consecutive evaluation periods before toggling states
Mitigation-3: Async evaluation path where routing decision uses last-known-good policy when control plane is delayed
Mitigation-4: Console and API surface show prominent status and send a profile_degradation webhook to customers
open_questions: Q1: What default thresholds should we recommend for 'low-latency' vs 'balanced' vs 'high-quality' profiles?
Q2: Should fallbacks be limited by model family (e.g., only choose within same architecture) or by semantic quality labels?
Q3: How to represent cost guidance in the profile schema (numeric per-token cap vs qualitative)?
Q4: Do enterprise customers require explicit opt-in for automatic fallback to ensure compliance?
notes: We should reuse earlier telemetry events defined for runtime-1.18 where possible to avoid schema churn
Design review scheduled with DEUX on 2026-03-12 to validate Console copy and simulation UX
Coordinate with Deploy and Dedicated teams to ensure fallbacks respect reserved capacity constraints
